chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from al-Qāsim ibn Ismāʿīl al-Anbārī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mihzam, from his father, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

We mentioned before him the kings of the family of so-and-so, so he said: People have only perished because of their hastening for this matter. Indeed, Allah does not hasten on account of the haste of the servants. Indeed, for this matter there is an end-point to which it will arrive; so if they had reached it, they would neither advance it by an hour nor delay it.

key_terms.اسْتِعْجَالِهِمْ: their seeking to hasten the matter before its appointed time
key_terms.الْأَمْرِ: the divinely ordained affair, in context the matter of the Imam
key_terms.غَايَةً: an appointed end-point or fixed term
key_terms.مُلُوكَ: kings or rulers being discussed in contrast to the divinely decreed affair
key_terms.هَلَكَ: perished or was ruined, referring to the spiritual harm caused by haste
key_terms.يَسْتَأْخِرُوا: delay or put back after its decreed time
key_terms.يَسْتَقْدِمُوا: bring forward or advance before its decreed time

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام forbid hastening or setting a time for the rise of al-Mahdi عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the divinely appointed matter, understood in context as the affair of the Imam and his rise, unfolds according to Allah’s fixed decree rather than human impatience. It warns against hastening and timing such events, affirming that their appointed end cannot be brought forward or delayed even by an hour.
